does: Presses a portion of warm cooked rice between wet, salted hands into a firm triangle, ball or barrel that holds together but is not packed hard.
how: Wet your hands in cold water, rub a little salt over the palms and shake off the excess.
Scoop up a portion of warm rice and press it lightly into a ball.
Turn it in the hollow of one hand while pressing the other hand into a corner or an edge, to form the shape. Add a filling in the middle first if it is wanted.
Squeeze only enough to hold it together, so that air stays between the grains.

cues.text: The rice holds together when lifted, and still feels light.
The shape has clean edges and a surface with no cracks.

mistakes.mistake: Packing the rice hard, which turns it dense and heavy.
Shaping with dry hands, so that the rice sticks to them.
mistakes.fix: Wet and salt your hands each time.

variant_of.differs: Warm cooked rice is shaped with wet, salted hands and kept light, so that the grains stay whole, not packed like a meat mixture.
